newsitem.title: UK: IPE losses hit already weak Med oil products.
newsitem.headline: IPE losses hit already weak Med oil products.

text.p: Med oil products were weakened by the fall in crude futures and lack of arb opportunities, traders said.
Gasoline fell in line with crude and unleaded gasoline futures in the U.S. although fresh demand in the region stemmed the falls somewhat.
Dealers reported a new need for 25,000 tonnes of 95 RON unleaded and 98 RON leaded gasoline for Slovenia in mid June.
A fresh Italian requirement was seen for 15-17,000 tonnes of leaded/unleaded gasoline for early/mid June arrival, and another for 20,000 tonnes of leaded/unleaded gasoline.
The dates for the second Italian requirement were not known.
Naphtha dealers said the market had fallen by around $5 a tonne, in line with the decline in cif NWE swaps.
Gas oil was also weaker as falls in IPE gas oil futures pressured an already fragile market. Premiums were still in negative territory around high cif quotes -$1.50/-$2.50 cif NWE.
Traders said prices looked set to remain weak for the time being, although some material appeared to being siphoned off into NWE which would help support prices, traders said.
Some of the Russian fuel weighing heavily on the market last week were reported to have been soaked up by refinery buying.
But while the Med fuel market was tighter future Russian flows looked ample and at least two cargoes were still on the water without buyers.

Dealers were looking to the Electricidade de Portugal high sulphur tender to buy two cargoes, with an option for a third, to liven up the market, but acknowledged the material would most likely be sourced from north-west Europe.
Egypt has also tendered to sell low sulphur straight-run in June, traders said.
